entry_rationale.why_sold_off: 737 MAX production quality issues re-emerged in 2024, FAA production cap imposed, CEO departure, multiple fatal incidents damaged brand, labor strike halted production for weeks. Stock fell from ~$265 to under $200.
entry_rationale.selloff_type: Company-specific operational issues, NOT secular demand decline. Air travel demand is structurally strong and growing. Boeing has a duopoly with Airbus — no substitute at scale.
entry_rationale.is_issue_fixable: Yes — new CEO Kelly Ortberg brought in to stabilize. Production certification issues fixable with time and investment. Backlog of 5,500+ aircraft (7-8 years of production) is intact and growing.
entry_rationale.balance_sheet: Highly levered (~$45B net debt), primary risk. BUT Boeing has access to capital markets, implicit government support as critical defense contractor, and backlog provides future cash flow visibility.
entry_rationale.industry_protection: Commercial aviation is structural growth industry globally. Defense segment (~30% of revenue) provides floor and is non-cyclical. FAA oversight barriers entry.
catalysts: 737 MAX production volume returning to 38/month target
New CEO execution credibility building over 4-6 quarters
entry_rationale.bear_case: Regulatory action escalates, another safety incident, financing costs become unsustainable. Low probability but existential.

valuation_at_entry.ev_ebitda: Difficult to calculate due to losses, but replacement cost of assets and backlog value implied massive discount

key_lessons: Duopoly businesses don't go away even in crisis
Management change is a powerful catalyst
Backlog / order book is the key valuation anchor for aerospace
High leverage is acceptable when revenue stream is contractual and long-cycle

entry_rationale.why_sold_off: Pain drug suzetrigine (VX-548) Phase 3 trial showed mixed results vs. opioids. Market concern about commercial penetration. Stock pulled back 25-30% from $530 highs.
entry_rationale.selloff_type: Pipeline disappointment on a single non-core asset (core franchise is cystic fibrosis, not pain). Market over-extrapolated from pain drug miss to entire franchise.
entry_rationale.is_issue_fixable: Partially — pain drug potential is uncertain. But irrelevant to core thesis: near-monopoly on CF treatments (Trikafta/Kaftrio), 85%+ eligible patient penetration with pricing power.
entry_rationale.balance_sheet: Net cash ~$10B. No debt. Extraordinary FCF generation. One of the cleanest balance sheets in large-cap pharma.
entry_rationale.industry_protection: CF drugs are not optional — patients die without them. Pricing power is durable. No competition exists at scale.
catalysts: Inaxaplin for APOL1 kidney disease Phase 3
entry_rationale.bear_case: IRA price negotiations target Trikafta. Biosimilar entry into CF (low probability). Multiple pipeline failures.

valuation_at_entry.forward_pe: 23x — premium but at discount to own history for a near-monopoly franchise

key_lessons: When the market punishes a stock for a non-core miss, check if core franchise is intact
Net cash balance sheets create a floor
Monopoly-like healthcare franchises deserve premium multiples
Look for situations where stock fell on 'fear of X' but X hasn't materialized in core numbers

entry_rationale.why_sold_off: Post-COVID demand normalization. Home standby generator demand fell sharply from 2020-2022 highs, dealer inventories bloated. Stock collapsed from $500 peak to $120-140.
entry_rationale.selloff_type: Classic post-cycle mean reversion. Underlying long-term demand drivers (grid unreliability, extreme weather, electrification) are STRUCTURAL. Selloff was about demand air pocket, not permanent loss.
entry_rationale.is_issue_fixable: Yes — dealer inventory normalization is time-limited. Once inventory clears, shipments re-align with true underlying demand. Climate change structurally supports above-pre-COVID demand.
entry_rationale.balance_sheet: Net debt but manageable (~2x EBITDA at trough). FCF positive throughout downturn. No near-term maturity concerns.
entry_rationale.industry_protection: Home standby generators are infrastructure-adjacent. Grid investment in US accelerating; data center power demand straining grids creates permanent tailwind for backup power.
entry_rationale.bear_case: Inventory takes longer to clear. Mild hurricane season. Competition from Kohler. But at $140, all priced in.

valuation_at_entry.forward_pe: 18x trough earnings — cheap for structural growth with moat

key_lessons: Post-cycle demand normalization is NOT a broken business
Best contrarian entries when narrative is 'COVID pull-forward is over' — find structural demand drivers
Inventory cycle turns are highly predictable
Strong brand + distribution moats survive demand air pockets
